title: Fluid dashboard and modal reflow for cross-browser parity
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Make key console pages (dashboards, rollout pages, cost views) reflow reliably across a broad set of viewports and browsers while preserving visual hierarchy, table legibility, chart integrity, and modal behavior.

Scope:
- Dashboard grid responsiveness: card wrapping, density controls, and minimum readable widths.
- Tables: column priority, responsive column collapsing rules, and sticky header behavior.
- Charts: maintain axis labels, responsive legends, and prevent clipping at smaller widths.
- Modals: center/anchored modes, stacked modal handling, and scroll lock semantics on mobile.
- Cross-browser fixes: address rendering differences in Safari/FF/Edge (particularly flex-min-height, subpixel aliasing on canvas charts, and backdrop-filter fallbacks).

Acceptance criteria summarized below. Must include prototypes and QA signoff in Chrome, Safari (macOS/iOS), Firefox, and Edge.

Constraints: design tokens must map to existing UI kit; minimize changes to runtime classnames to avoid large engineering refactors.
comments: 2026-02-22 Maya Chen: Initial discovery complete. Pulled telemetry for smallest 5% viewport widths from Console analytics dashboard — main pain points are table horizontal scroll and chart label overlap.

2026-02-25 Priya Nair (Eng): Confirmed table column-priority API is available in table component; engineering suggests we avoid removing columns entirely, prefer collapsing to stacked rows for mobile.
2026-03-01 Ryan Gomez (PM): Prioritizing dashboards and rollout pages for this cycle; cost view can be staged if timeboxed. Added to Console UX Refresh Q1 2026 project.

2026-03-04 Omar Patel: Prototype updated with fluid 12-column grid and density toggle. Implemented sticky header spec and provided CSS fallback for -webkit-backdrop-filter. Pushed notes to the drive spec.
2026-03-07 Lucas Zhao (UX Research): Quick hallway usability test (n=8) — users expect charts to preserve Y-axis tick readability; suggested reducing legend size before truncating axis labels.

2026-03-09 Design review: Team agreed on priority order for table columns, and to defer full table virtualization changes to an ENG ticket. Need engineering signoff for modal scroll-lock implementation.

2026-03-11 QA (Tristan): Cross-browser smoke in staging: Firefox had 1px off-by-one canvas render on stacked area chart; created ENG bug ENG-2489. Safari on iOS shows backdrop opacity differences — applied fallback color per spec.
2026-03-12 Omar Patel: Implemented rounding fix for canvas rendering and added a conditional legend collapse at <= 420px. Updated prototype links and requested final design review on 2026-03-15.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard cards reflow cleanly at breakpoints 1280px, 1024px, 768px, and 420px with no horizontal scroll introduced
Tables use defined column-priority rules; at <=540px collapsed row view is present and readable; sticky header remains functional
Charts preserve axis labels or collapse legends; no clipping of data marks at smaller widths; visual regression diff passes baseline
Modals respect stacking order, body scroll lock for mobile, and keyboard accessibility for focus trap
No visual regressions across Chrome (latest), Safari (macOS + iOS), Firefox, and Edge. QA signoff recorded with screenshots in Drive
ui_kit_updates: grid: switch default to fluid 12 columns
spacing: add spacing-6 for compact cards
notes_for_engineering: Prefer CSS grid for dashboard composition; fall back to flex for older environments where necessary
Avoid heavy DOM changes — use CSS transforms where possible for sticky behavior
Provide explicit pixel-aligned canvas drawing to fix subpixel aliasing in Firefox
Expose a table 'columnPriority' prop to map to the design's mobile collapse sequence
